projects.title: Project 3: Smoothie Menu Filter 🥤

cells.markdown:

projects.title: Project 6: Inventory Restock Alert 📦
projects.description: Find products that need restocking.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — Below reorder point

qty less than reorder_at means restock.
cells.source:
SELECT sku, item, qty, reorder_at
FROM inventory
WHERE qty < reorder_at
ORDER BY qty;

projects.title: Project 7: Library Card Between 📚
projects.description: Find books in a page-count range with BETWEEN.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — Mid-length reads

BETWEEN is inclusive on both ends.
cells.source:
SELECT title, pages, genre
FROM books
WHERE pages BETWEEN 100 AND 300
ORDER BY pages;

projects.title: Project 8: Tag Search Like 🔎
projects.description: Pattern-match product tags with LIKE.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — Apparel tags

`%` matches any sequence of characters.
cells.source:
SELECT name, tag
FROM products
WHERE tag LIKE 'apparel%'
ORDER BY name;

projects.title: Project 9: Null Detector Agency 🕵️
projects.description: Hunt missing emails with IS NULL.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — Missing contacts

NULL means unknown — compare with IS NULL, not `= NULL`.
cells.source:
SELECT name
FROM members
WHERE email IS NULL
ORDER BY name;

projects.title: Project 10: Alias Nickname Studio 🎭
projects.description: Rename columns and computed fields with AS.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — Friendly result headers

Aliases make result grids readable.
cells.source:
SELECT event AS show_name,
       price AS seat_price,
       qty AS seats,
       price * qty AS line_total
FROM tickets
ORDER BY line_total DESC;

projects.title: Project 11: Ticket Counter Aggregate 🎫
projects.description: Summarize a sales table with COUNT, SUM, AVG.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — One-row summary

Aggregates collapse many rows into stats.
cells.source:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders,
       SUM(amount) AS revenue,
       ROUND(AVG(amount), 2) AS avg_order,
       MIN(amount) AS cheapest,
       MAX(amount) AS biggest
FROM sales;

projects.title: Project 12: Genre Group Party 🎧
projects.description: Count songs per genre with GROUP BY.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — Songs per genre

GROUP BY buckets rows before aggregating.
cells.source:
SELECT genre, COUNT(*) AS tracks, ROUND(AVG(duration_sec)) AS avg_sec
FROM songs
GROUP BY genre
ORDER BY tracks DESC;

projects.title: Project 13: Having Heroes Only 🦸
projects.description: Filter groups after aggregation with HAVING.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — Strong teams

WHERE filters rows; HAVING filters groups.
cells.source:
SELECT team, COUNT(*) AS members, ROUND(AVG(power), 1) AS avg_power
FROM heroes
GROUP BY team
HAVING AVG(power) >= 80
ORDER BY avg_power DESC;

projects.title: Project 14: Inner Join Buddy Film 🎬
projects.description: Connect movies to directors with INNER JOIN.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — Movies with known directors

INNER JOIN keeps only matching pairs.
cells.source:
SELECT m.title, d.name AS director
FROM movies AS m
INNER JOIN directors AS d ON d.id = m.director_id
ORDER BY m.title;

projects.title: Project 15: Left Join Waitlist 🕓
projects.description: Keep all customers even when orders are missing.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — Who has not ordered?

LEFT JOIN keeps left-table rows; filter where right side is NULL.
cells.source:
SELECT c.name, o.item
FROM customers AS c
LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id
ORDER BY c.name, o.item;

cells.markdown:
### Step 2 — Customers with zero orders

Same join, keep unmatched customers only.
cells.source:
SELECT c.name AS no_order_yet
FROM customers AS c
LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE o.id IS NULL;

projects.title: Project 16: Multi Table Quest Log 🗺️
projects.description: Join heroes, quests, and completions across three tables.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — Who finished what

Chain JOINs with clear aliases.
cells.source:
SELECT h.name AS hero, q.title AS quest, q.xp, c.stars
FROM completions AS c
JOIN heroes AS h ON h.id = c.hero_id
JOIN quests AS q ON q.id = c.quest_id
ORDER BY h.name, q.xp DESC;

projects.title: Project 17: Subquery Treasure Hunt 🪙
projects.description: Find chests richer than the average using a subquery.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — Above-average loot

A subquery in WHERE returns one value here.
cells.source:
SELECT label, gold
FROM chests
WHERE gold > (SELECT AVG(gold) FROM chests)
ORDER BY gold DESC;

projects.title: Project 19: Case When Mood Ring 💍
projects.description: Bucket numeric scores into labels with CASE.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — Letter mood grades

CASE turns numbers into readable categories.
cells.source:
SELECT student, score,
  CASE
    WHEN score >= 90 THEN 'glowing'
    WHEN score >= 80 THEN 'bright'
    WHEN score >= 70 THEN 'warming'
    ELSE 'needs charge'
  END AS mood
FROM quizzes
ORDER BY score DESC;

projects.title: Project 20: Union Band Playlist 🎸
projects.description: Stack two set lists with UNION.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — Combined unique tracks

UNION removes duplicates; UNION ALL keeps them.
cells.source:
SELECT track FROM set_a
UNION
SELECT track FROM set_b
ORDER BY track;

cells.markdown:
### Step 2 — Keep duplicates (ALL)

See overlapping songs appear twice.
cells.source:
SELECT track FROM set_a
UNION ALL
SELECT track FROM set_b
ORDER BY track;

projects.title: Project 28: Upsert Score Patch 🩹
projects.description: Insert or replace a player's best score.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — Upsert higher scores only

ON CONFLICT patches an existing primary key.
cells.source:
INSERT INTO best_scores (player, points) VALUES ('Nova', 940)
ON CONFLICT(player) DO UPDATE SET
  points = CASE
    WHEN excluded.points > best_scores.points THEN excluded.points
    ELSE best_scores.points
  END;
INSERT INTO best_scores (player, points) VALUES ('Rio', 880)
ON CONFLICT(player) DO UPDATE SET
  points = CASE
    WHEN excluded.points > best_scores.points THEN excluded.points
    ELSE best_scores.points
  END;
SELECT * FROM best_scores ORDER BY points DESC;

projects.title: Project 29: Window Rank Race 🏁
projects.description: Rank racers with window functions.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — Rank within each lane

Window functions compute across related rows without collapsing them.
cells.source:
SELECT racer, lane, seconds,
       RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY lane ORDER BY seconds) AS place
FROM race_times
ORDER BY lane, place, racer;

projects.title: Project 30: CTE Trail Map 🧭
projects.description: Build a readable query with a WITH clause (CTE).

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — Long hard trails via CTE

CTEs name intermediate results for clarity.
cells.source:
WITH hard AS (
  SELECT trail, km FROM hikes WHERE difficulty = 'hard'
)
SELECT trail, km
FROM hard
WHERE km >= 10
ORDER BY km DESC;

projects.title: Project 31: Date Festival Filter 📅
projects.description: Work with date strings and SQLite date functions.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — July events after the 12th

Store dates as ISO text `YYYY-MM-DD` for easy sorting.
cells.source:
SELECT name, starts_on,
       CAST(julianday(starts_on) - julianday('2026-07-12') AS INTEGER) AS days_after_jul12
FROM events
WHERE starts_on LIKE '2026-07%'
  AND starts_on > '2026-07-12'
ORDER BY starts_on;

  lower(trim(label)) AS slug,
  upper(substr(trim(label), 1, 1)) || lower(substr(trim(label), 2)) AS titled,
  length(trim(label)) AS chars

projects.title: Project 35: Recursive Org Chart 🏢
projects.description: Walk a management tree with a recursive CTE.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — Everyone under Eng Lead

Recursive CTEs follow parent/child links.
cells.source:
WITH RECURSIVE reports AS (
  SELECT id, name, manager_id, 0 AS depth
  FROM staff WHERE name = 'Eng Lead'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT s.id, s.name, s.manager_id, r.depth + 1
  FROM staff AS s
  JOIN reports AS r ON s.manager_id = r.id
)
SELECT depth, name FROM reports ORDER BY depth, name;

projects.title: Project 36: Pivot Ish Crosstab 📊
projects.description: Fake a pivot table with conditional aggregation.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — Course flags per student

Conditional SUM turns rows into columns.
cells.source:
SELECT student,
  SUM(CASE WHEN course = 'SQL' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS took_sql,
  SUM(CASE WHEN course = 'HTML' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS took_html,
  SUM(CASE WHEN course = 'JS' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS took_js
FROM enroll
GROUP BY student
ORDER BY student;

projects.title: Project 37: Many To Many Playlist 🎶
projects.description: Model songs ↔ playlists with a junction table.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — Songs on Focus

Join through the junction table.
cells.source:
SELECT p.name AS playlist, s.title AS song
FROM playlist_songs AS ps
JOIN playlists AS p ON p.id = ps.playlist_id
JOIN songs AS s ON s.id = ps.song_id
WHERE p.name = 'Focus'
ORDER BY s.title;

projects.title: Project 38: Report Dashboard Query 📈
projects.description: Build a compact sales dashboard with joins + aggregates.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — Revenue by city & category

A classic dashboard-shaped query.
cells.source:
SELECT c.city, p.category,
       SUM(oi.qty) AS units,
       ROUND(SUM(oi.qty * p.price), 2) AS revenue
FROM order_items AS oi
JOIN customers AS c ON c.id = oi.customer_id
JOIN products AS p ON p.id = oi.product_id
GROUP BY c.city, p.category
ORDER BY c.city, revenue DESC;

projects.title: Project 39: Data Cleanup Detox 🧽
projects.description: Clean messy imports with TRIM, CAST, and NULLIF.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — Normalize for analysis

NULLIF turns blank strings into NULL.
cells.source:
SELECT
  trim(raw_name) AS name,
  CAST(NULLIF(lower(trim(raw_age)), 'n/a') AS INTEGER) AS age
FROM messy
WHERE trim(raw_name) <> ''
ORDER BY name;

projects.title: Project 40: Capstone Shop Analytics 🏪
projects.description: Capstone: explore a tiny shop schema with joins, windows, and CTEs.

cells.markdown:
### Step 1 — Customer lifetime value

CTE + join + window for a shop snapshot.
cells.source:
WITH line_rev AS (
  SELECT o.customer_id,
         o.id AS order_id,
         SUM(ol.qty * p.price) AS order_total
  FROM orders AS o
  JOIN order_lines AS ol ON ol.order_id = o.id
  JOIN products AS p ON p.id = ol.product_id
  GROUP BY o.customer_id, o.id
),
cust AS (
  SELECT customer_id,
         COUNT(*) AS orders,
         ROUND(SUM(order_total), 2) AS revenue
  FROM line_rev
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT c.name, c.cohort, cust.orders, cust.revenue,
       ROUND(cust.revenue * 1.0 / cust.orders, 2) AS avg_order,
       RANK() OVER (ORDER BY cust.revenue DESC) AS revenue_rank
FROM cust
JOIN customers AS c ON c.id = cust.customer_id
ORDER BY revenue_rank;
